The best Indian restaurant in Phu Quoc.
Feb 2020 • Solo
This restaurant was recommended to me as the best Indian restaurant in Phu Quoc and it did not disappoint ! I do not eat animal products and find it rather challenging to find a restaurant here that would cater to my dietary needs. But I found my happiness at Spice India! I order the vegetable shashlik (if you are vegan, specify you don’t want them to add paneer to the brochette) and the Manchuria mushrooms. The food was delicious, very taste, with just the right amount of spice and exquisite flavors. The naan was fluffy, chewy and warm. I will definitely go back before the end of my stay. A little pricey but highly recommended !

Food ok, service shocking
Jan 2020 • Couples
Ate here with my partner one evening after seeing good reviews on Tripadvisor however our experience seemed completely the opposite!

It was clear from the start that the waiter didn't want to serve us at all, refused to even ask the chef if they could do a Chicken Tikka Korma (usually a very simple request in an indian restaurant).

Ordered starters and mains however I guess he couldn't be bothered doing two trips to the kitchen as he brought everything at once.

The food it's self was ok, nothing special. Popadoms tasted stale and the Currys we ordered were a bit bland.

Waiter didn't even make eye contact for the rest of the meal and completely ignored us when we tried to get his attention to get extra drinks or even when we wanted to pay.

There are better Indian restaurants a few minutes walk from here so avoid this place at all costs.

Food was decent, not deserving of 4.5 stars though
Jan 2020
Went here for dinner with my bf. I ordered the veg thali and he got butter chicken and some bread. The waitress made a massive point of asking me how spicy I wanted my food and I made the point back that indeed I wanted it spicy. All of this was ridiculous considering not a single curry that came in the thali ended up spicy at all. Anyways. The dal and raita were pretty good. The other curries were meh - mostly just potatoes. The rice wasn't basmati. I tasted my bf's butter chicken and it didn't taste anything like what I've had before in India or otherwise. Mainly it was very sweet which I found strange. The gulab jamun that came in the thali was SOOOOOOO far from what gulab jamun usually tastes like (no cardamon, no rose water), I couldn't eat it, and I love that dessert! Anyway, it was an okay meal but I'm not sure why they have such outstanding reviews.
